rows.question: How many days do I have to submit a reimbursement claim after discharge?
rows.answer: For standard claims, you must submit the reimbursement claim within 30 days of discharge [1][2]. For Aurora Group Health corporate plans, the submission window is 60 days from discharge [4].
rows.gold_answer: 30 days from the date of discharge.

rows.question: What is the room rent limit on the Silver plan?
rows.answer: The room rent limit on the Aurora Silver plan is 2% of the sum insured per day [3][4].
rows.gold_answer: 2% of the sum insured per day.

rows.question: Is maternity covered on the Bronze plan?
rows.answer: No, maternity is not covered on the Bronze plan at any sum insured [1][2].
rows.gold_answer: No. Maternity is not available on Bronze at any sum insured; it is available on Silver, Gold and Platinum.

rows.question: What is the waiting period for pre-existing diseases?
rows.answer: The waiting period for pre-existing diseases is generally 36 months on standard retail plans, top-up plans, and hospital cash benefits [3][5][7][9][10]. However, under the Aurora Senior Care plan for ages 60 and above, the pre-existing disease waiting period is 24 months [5].
rows.gold_answer: 36 months of continuous coverage. A rider can reduce it to 24 or 12 months if bought at inception or first renewal.

rows.question: How long is the grace period for an annual policy?
rows.answer: The grace period for an annual policy is **30 days** from the renewal due date [1][5].
rows.gold_answer: 30 days for annual policies (15 days for instalment policies). Cover does not operate during the grace period; it only preserves continuity of waiting periods and no-claim bonus.

rows.question: How many hospitals are in the Aurora network?
rows.answer: As of 1 April 2026, Aurora's network covers 11,400 hospitals across 780 towns [1].
rows.gold_answer: 11,400 hospitals across 780 towns as of 1 April 2026, though the app locator is the authoritative live list.

rows.question: What is the no-claim bonus on Gold?
rows.answer: Under Aurora Gold, the no-claim bonus is 25% of the base sum insured per claim-free year, accumulating to a maximum of 100% [1][5]. A claim does not reduce the accumulated bonus; it only stops accumulating for that specific year [1].
rows.gold_answer: 25% of base sum insured per claim-free year, accumulating to a maximum of 100%. A claim stops accumulation for that year but does not reduce the bonus.

rows.question: Can I claim for IVF treatment?
rows.answer: No, you cannot claim for IVF treatment. Infertility, assisted reproduction, and IVF are listed as permanent exclusions [1].
rows.gold_answer: No. Infertility treatment, assisted reproduction and IVF are permanent exclusions on all plans.

rows.question: What is the cataract sub-limit on Gold?
rows.answer: Under the Aurora Gold plan, the sub-limit for cataract surgery is ₹75,000 per eye [1].
rows.gold_answer: Rs 75,000 per eye.

rows.question: Who can I escalate to if Aurora rejects my claim and their internal response is unsatisfactory?
rows.answer: If you are not satisfied with the initial (Stage 1) outcome, you can escalate to Aurora's Grievance Redressal Officer [2]. If Aurora's final response is unsatisfactory, you may approach the Insurance Ombudsman for your region [1].
rows.gold_answer: Escalate to Aurora's Grievance Redressal Officer (14-day response), then to the Insurance Ombudsman for your region within 1 year of the final rejection.

rows.question: How much ambulance cover is there?
rows.answer: Across all plans, road ambulance cover is ₹5,000 per hospitalisation [1][6][9]. In addition, the Gold plan provides air ambulance cover up to ₹2,50,000 per policy year within India, subject to prior authorisation [5].
rows.gold_answer: Rs 5,000 per hospitalisation for road ambulance on all plans. Gold and Platinum additionally cover air ambulance up to Rs 2,50,000 per year within India on prior authorisation.

rows.question: Is mental illness covered?
rows.answer: Yes, in-patient treatment for mental illness is covered on the same terms as physical illness [1]. It is subject to the standard 30-day initial waiting period, with no separate waiting period required [1].
rows.gold_answer: Yes. In-patient treatment for mental illness is covered on the same terms as physical illness under the Mental Healthcare Act 2017, subject only to the 30-day initial waiting period.

rows.question: What is the free-look period?
rows.answer:
The free-look period is the window in which a new policyholder can cancel/return a new policy for a refund [2][3]. It lasts **15 days** from receiving the policy document, or **30 days** if the policy was sold through distance marketing [1][2]. 

If cancelled within this period, the premium is refunded minus proportionate risk premium for the period of cover, medical examination costs, and stamp duty [2].
rows.gold_answer: 15 days from receipt of the policy document, or 30 days if sold through distance marketing.

rows.question: How many wellness points do I get for completing an annual health check-up?
rows.answer: You get 150 wellness points for completing an annual health check-up [1].
rows.gold_answer: 150 points.

rows.question: What is a day-care procedure?
rows.answer: A day-care procedure is a medical procedure that requires less than 24 hours of hospitalisation due to technological advances, making it payable despite the general 24-hour admission requirement [3]. Out-patient treatment is not considered a day-care procedure [3].
rows.gold_answer: A procedure requiring less than 24 hours of hospitalisation due to technological advance, and therefore payable despite the general 24-hour admission requirement. Out-patient treatment is not a day-care procedure.

rows.question: Within how many hours must a hospital notify Aurora of an emergency admission for cashless?
rows.answer: For an emergency admission under the cashless route, the hospital must notify Aurora within **24 hours** of admission [1][5].
rows.gold_answer: Within 24 hours of admission.

rows.question: Does Aurora use a TPA?
rows.answer: No, Aurora administers its own claims and does not use a Third Party Administrator (TPA) [1].
rows.gold_answer: No. Aurora administers its own claims and does not use a Third Party Administrator.

rows.question: What is the minimum number of beds a facility needs to count as a hospital?
rows.answer: To qualify as a hospital under the policy, a facility must have at least 10 in-patient beds in towns with a population below 10 lakh, or at least 15 in-patient beds elsewhere [1].
rows.gold_answer: At least 10 in-patient beds in towns with a population below 10 lakh, and at least 15 elsewhere.

rows.question: I am on Silver with a 5 lakh sum insured and took a room at Rs 15,000 per day. Will everything be paid?
rows.answer: No, everything will not be paid. Under the Silver plan with a ₹5,00,000 sum insured, your room-rent limit is 2% (₹10,000 per day) [1][2]. Because you exceeded this limit by taking a room at ₹15,000 per day, a proportionate deduction (eligibility ratio of 0.667) will be applied to the room rent and all associated charges tied to the room category, resulting in out-of-pocket expenses [1][5][8]. Only pharmacy and consumables are exempt from proportionate reduction [8].
rows.gold_answer: No. The Silver room-rent limit is 2% of 5,00,000 = Rs 10,000/day, so an eligibility ratio of 0.667 is applied by proportionate deduction to all room-linked charges (room, surgeon, anaesthetist, nursing, OT, investigations). Pharmacy and consumables are not reduced.

rows.question: My mother is 63 and I want to add her to my policy. Which plans allow it and what changes?
rows.answer:
You can add a dependent parent to the **Silver** (at an extra premium), **Gold**, and **Platinum** plans; the **Bronze** plan does not allow it [1]. 

When you add her, the following changes occur:
- **Premium calculation**: The overall policy premium is determined by the age of the eldest covered member (your mother at 63), which often increases the cost [4].
- **Co-payment**: On the Silver plan, a 10% co-payment will apply to every claim because the eldest insured member is over 60 [8]. (Any co-payment rules for Gold or Platinum for members over 60 are not stated in the provided sources).
rows.gold_answer: Dependent parents can be added on Silver (at extra premium), Gold and Platinum, but not on Bronze. Premium is set by the eldest member's age, and on Silver a 10% co-payment applies to every claim once the eldest insured is above 60. Aurora must present a separate senior-citizen policy as an alternative in writing.

rows.question: I am switching from another insurer. Will my 3 years of waiting period carry over if I increase my sum insured?
rows.answer: Yes, the waiting periods you have already served will carry over, but only up to the sum insured of your previous policy (including accrued no-claim bonus) [1][2][6]. Any increase or incremental sum insured beyond that amount will be subject to fresh waiting periods [1][2].
rows.gold_answer: Waiting-period credit carries over only up to the sum insured of the previous policy including its accrued no-claim bonus. The incremental sum insured is subject to fresh waiting periods. Apply 45-60 days before the existing renewal date.

rows.question: My baby was born last week. What do I need to do and by when?
rows.answer:
To ensure your baby remains covered:

* **Add the baby to the policy:** You must inform Aurora within **90 days of birth** to add your newborn as a dependent [1]. Adding them within this 90-day window is guaranteed-issue with no medical underwriting; after 90 days, the child is treated as a fresh applicant [1]. (Your newborn is already covered under the maternity limit for the first 90 days from birth [2]).
* **File reimbursement claims (if applicable):** If you are submitting a reimbursement claim for hospitalisation, you must submit it within **30 days of discharge**, and post-hospitalisation bills within **15 days** after the post-hospitalisation period ends [3][7].
rows.gold_answer: The newborn is covered from day one within the maternity limit for the first 90 days. To continue cover beyond that, inform Aurora and add the child as a dependent within 90 days of birth, which is guaranteed-issue with no medical underwriting. After 90 days the child is treated as a fresh applicant.

rows.question: Can I get an out-patient physiotherapy session reimbursed on Bronze?
rows.answer: The Out-Patient (OPD) rider is not available on the Bronze plan [1]. Specific coverage or reimbursement for out-patient physiotherapy is not mentioned in the provided sources.
rows.gold_answer: No. Out-patient treatment is not covered under any base plan, and the OPD rider is not available on Bronze.

rows.question: I had a claim last year on Silver. What happens to my accumulated no-claim bonus?
rows.answer: Under the Aurora Silver plan, making a claim reduces your accumulated no-claim bonus by 10 percentage points; it is not reset to zero [1].
rows.gold_answer: On Silver a claim reduces the accumulated bonus by 10 percentage points; it does not reset to zero. Silver accrues 10% per claim-free year up to 50%.

rows.question: How much would a caesarean cost me out of pocket on Gold if the hospital bills 1,60,000?
rows.answer: Under the Gold plan, the maternity sub-limit for a Caesarean section is ₹1,00,000 [1]. Because proportionate deduction does not apply on Gold [8], you would pay **₹60,000** out of pocket on a ₹1,60,000 bill (₹1,60,000 minus the ₹1,00,000 policy limit) [1][8].
rows.gold_answer: The Gold caesarean limit is Rs 1,00,000 per delivery, so approximately Rs 60,000 is out of pocket. Gold has no co-payment. Pre-natal care in the 30 days before and post-natal care for 60 days after draw down the same limit.

rows.question: Is knee replacement covered immediately after I buy the policy?
rows.answer: No, knee joint replacement has a 24-month waiting period unless it is required following an accident [1][5]. Claims resulting from accidental injury are covered immediately from day one [2][5].
rows.gold_answer: No. Knee and hip joint replacement other than following an accident carries a 24-month waiting period. Sub-limits also apply: Rs 1,50,000 per joint on Bronze, Rs 2,50,000 on Silver, none on Gold.

rows.question: What is the total maximum discount I can get on premium?
rows.answer: Total discounts are capped at 30% of the base premium [1]. However, the wellness discount (up to 15% at renewal) is applied last, after the cap, and is the only discount that may exceed it [1][3][5]—allowing for a total maximum discount of up to 45%.
rows.gold_answer: Discounts are capped at 30% of base premium, but the wellness discount of up to 15% is applied after the cap and is the only discount permitted to exceed it.

rows.question: I want cashless at a hospital that turns out to be an excluded provider. What are my options?
rows.answer: Cashless access is not available at an excluded provider and will be denied [2][3]. Your only option is to pay and file for reimbursement [1][3][5], which requires pre-approval [3] and is payable only if the admission was a genuine emergency and no alternative facility was reachable [1].
rows.gold_answer: Cashless is not available at an excluded provider. The claim is payable on reimbursement only if the admission was a genuine emergency with no reachable alternative facility, and pre-approval is required.

rows.question: How many days do I have to respond to a query Aurora raises on my claim?
rows.answer:
The deadline depends on the type of policy:

* **General/Health claims:** You have **45 days** from the date of the query to respond; if not received within 45 days, Aurora closes the claim [2][5][11].
* **Motor insurance claims:** You have **30 days** from the date of the query to respond [4].
rows.gold_answer: 45 days from the date of the query, under the rules effective 1 April 2026. (The archived 2024 document says 30 days and must not be quoted for current policies.)

rows.question: How far in advance must a planned cashless admission be notified?
rows.answer: For a planned cashless admission, the pre-authorisation request/notification must be submitted at least **72 hours** before admission [1][2].
rows.gold_answer: 72 hours before admission under the current rules. (The archived 2024 document says 48 hours.)

rows.question: How long does Aurora take to settle a reimbursement claim?
rows.answer:
Aurora settles or rejects a health reimbursement claim within **15 working days** of receiving the last required document (the clock restarts if a query is raised and the queried document is supplied) [1][2]. 

For other types of claims:
- **Hospital Cash Benefit:** Settled within 7 working days of the indemnity claim being settled [8].
- **Motor Insurance:** Settled or rejected within 30 days of the surveyor report [7].
rows.gold_answer: 15 working days from receipt of the last required document. (The archived 2024 document says 30 days.)

rows.question: Which plans have no co-payment?
rows.answer:
Based on the provided sources:

* **Aurora Gold** has nil (no) co-payment at all ages [1].
* **Aurora Silver** has no co-payment for members below age 60 (a 10% co-payment applies above age 60) [2].
* Two higher-tier variants of the **Aurora Group Health Corporate Plans** also have nil co-payment [6] (with two retail plan tiers also listing nil co-payment [4]).
rows.gold_answer: Gold and Platinum have nil co-payment at all ages. Bronze applies 20% and Silver 10% where the eldest insured is above 60.

rows.question: Compare the pre- and post-hospitalisation windows across all four plans.
rows.answer:
Across the four plans, the pre- and post-hospitalisation coverage windows are [1]:

* **Plan 1:** 30 days pre-hospitalisation and 60 days post-hospitalisation
* **Plan 2:** 45 days pre-hospitalisation and 90 days post-hospitalisation
* **Plan 3:** 60 days pre-hospitalisation and 120 days post-hospitalisation
* **Plan 4:** 90 days pre-hospitalisation and 180 days post-hospitalisation

*(Note: The specific plan names for these columns are not provided in the sources [1]).*
rows.gold_answer: Pre/post: Bronze 30/60 days, Silver 45/90, Gold 60/120, Platinum 90/180.

rows.question: Which plan should I buy if I want no room-rent sub-limit and cover for my parents-in-law?
rows.answer:
You should consider the **Gold** or **Platinum** plan:

* **Cover for parents-in-law:** Both Gold and Platinum allow coverage for dependent parents-in-law [1].
* **No room-rent sub-limit:** Gold removes room-rent sub-limits entirely (permitting any single private room) [3][6][8], while Platinum offers no room-rent limit (with suites excluded) [8].
rows.gold_answer: Gold (or Platinum). Gold removes room-rent and ICU sub-limits and is the lowest tier that permits dependent parents-in-law.

rows.question: List everything that is excluded relating to dental treatment.
rows.answer: Under Aurora indemnity plans, dental treatment, oral surgery, and out-patient dental work are excluded, unless the dental treatment or oral surgery is necessitated by an accidental injury requiring hospitalisation [1][2][3].
rows.gold_answer: Dental treatment and oral surgery are excluded unless necessitated by accidental injury requiring hospitalisation. One dental check-up and cleaning per year is covered under the optional OPD rider.

rows.answer: The specific helpline phone number is not stated in the provided sources, but it can be found on your policy schedule [1].

rows.question: If I skip paying on time, how long before I lose everything I've built up?
rows.answer:
For health insurance, you lose accumulated benefits (waiting periods restart, accumulated no-claim bonus is lost, and wellness points are forfeited) if you do not pay within the grace period, which is **30 days** for annual policies and **15 days** for instalment policies [1][2][12]. 

For life insurance, the policy lapses after the grace period (**30 days** for annual, half-yearly, or quarterly; **15 days** for monthly) [4][7]. However, an endowment policy that has acquired a surrender value does not lose everything, but instead continues as a paid-up policy with a reduced sum assured [7].
rows.gold_answer: You have a 30-day grace period (15 days for instalments) to renew without losing waiting-period continuity and no-claim bonus. Beyond it the policy is treated as fresh: waiting periods restart and the bonus is lost.

rows.question: The hospital said they won't do cashless. Am I finished?
rows.answer: No. Denial of cashless is **not** a rejection of the claim [1]. When cashless is denied, you can pay and file for reimbursement [3][6], where your claim is assessed against the full document set rather than just a pre-authorisation form [6]. In fact, a material proportion of denied cashless requests are subsequently settled on reimbursement [6].
rows.gold_answer: No. Denial of cashless is not a rejection of the claim. You can pay and file for reimbursement, where the same facts are assessed against the full document set; a material proportion of denied cashless requests are later settled.

rows.question: My dad smoked for years and quit through your programme. Does that get me anything?
rows.answer: Completing a quit-tobacco programme earns 200 wellness points per year [2]. These points convert toward a renewal-premium discount at a rate of 1,000 points for a 5% discount (capped at 15%) [3].
rows.gold_answer: Completing the quit-tobacco programme earns 200 wellness points. Points convert at 1,000 points = 5% renewal discount, capped at 15%.

rows.question: AUR-HI-SIL-2026 — what are the sum insured options?
rows.answer: For product UIN AUR-HI-SIL-2026 (Aurora Silver) [2], the sum insured options are ₹5,00,000 (₹5L) and ₹10,00,000 (₹10L) [7][8].

rows.question: Is a 6 dioptre lasik covered?
rows.answer: No, refractive error correction is permanently excluded where the error is less than 7.5 dioptres [1]. Therefore, a 6 dioptre procedure is not covered [1].
rows.gold_answer: No. Refractive error correction is excluded where the error is less than 7.5 dioptres.
